questions.text: Why stream partial Thinker output into a Talker instead of waiting for the complete text response?

options.A: So speech synthesis can start while the Thinker continues composing the response.
options.B: So the Talker can avoid producing any speech tokens until the turn ends.
options.C: So all input audio can be discarded before the Thinker processes it.
options.D: So the waveform decoder can be removed from the speech pipeline.

questions.explanation: Incremental handoff overlaps response composition and speech synthesis, reducing the wait for first audio compared with completing all text first.

questions.text: An audio codec requires 50 base speech tokens for each second of playback. What sustained production rate must the Talker meet to avoid falling behind?

options.A: At most 25 base tokens per second.
options.B: Any positive rate, provided the first token arrives quickly.
options.C: At least 50 base tokens per second.
options.D: Exactly one base token for the entire response.

questions.explanation: Real-time playback consumes 50 base tokens each second, so sustained generation must meet or exceed that rate; low first-token latency alone does not prevent later underruns.

questions.text: The VAD simulator sets user stop=3800 ms and first audio=3800+silence_threshold_ms+400. With a 200 ms silence threshold, what is the lag from user stop to first audio?
questions.explanation: First audio is at 4400 ms; subtract the 3800 ms stop time to get 600 ms. The silence threshold adds to the later 400 ms delay.
